key_insight: Nominally cubic CsGeBr3 hosts long-lived, one-dimensional polar chains despite having zero net polarization.
engineering_relevance: These slow local polarization dynamics could inform halide-perovskite device modeling, although photovoltaic performance was not evaluated.
method: Analysis of polar correlations and polarization reversal
evidence_signal: Simulations reveal chains extending at least tens of nanometers and relaxing on nanosecond timescales—four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3—with chain-by-chain reversal in ferroelectric CsGeBr3.
watch_item: Experimental validation and the impact of these simulated dynamics on solar-cell operation remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
